description: There are n children standing in a line. Each child is assigned a rating value. You are giving candies to these children with the rules: each child must have at least one candy, and children with a higher rating than their neighbors must get more candies. Return the minimum total number of candies.
intuition: Two separate scans capture the two constraints independently. Left-to-right ensures higher-rated children get more than their left neighbor; right-to-left ensures the same for the right neighbor. Taking the maximum of both scans at each position satisfies both constraints simultaneously.
approach: Two-pass greedy. First pass left-to-right: if rating increases, give one more candy than the left neighbor. Second pass right-to-left: if rating increases going right, ensure more candies than the right neighbor. Take the max at each position.
jsWalkthrough:
Input: ratings = [1,0,2]

Initialize: candies = [1, 1, 1]

Left pass:
  i=1: ratings[1]=0 > ratings[0]=1? No -> candies[1]=1
  i=2: ratings[2]=2 > ratings[1]=0? Yes -> candies[2]=candies[1]+1=2
  candies = [1, 1, 2]

Right pass:
  i=1: ratings[1]=0 > ratings[2]=2? No -> candies[1]=1
  i=0: ratings[0]=1 > ratings[1]=0? Yes
    candies[0] = max(candies[0], candies[1]+1) = max(1, 2) = 2
  candies = [2, 1, 2]

Sum: 2+1+2 = 5

Output: 5
explanation:
1. Initialize all children with 1 candy.
2. Left pass: if rating[i] > rating[i-1], give more than left neighbor.
3. Right pass: if rating[i] > rating[i+1], ensure more than right neighbor.
4. Use max to satisfy both directions simultaneously.
5. Sum all candies for the minimum total.
hints: Each child must have more candies than neighbors with lower ratings.
One pass handles left neighbors, another handles right neighbors.
Take the maximum from both passes at each position.

phases.label: Enforce increasing ratings from the left
